subject: derived stats and variables not in frame

messages.author: daf017f67eba24e8
messages.subject: derived stats and variables not in frame
parts:
I appear to have troubles with the following conversion

ggplot( frame, aes(x=x, y=(..density..)*2) )

to

mult=2
ggplot( frame, aes(x=x, y=(..density..)*mult) )

it complains that mult is not found. I assume that's because it's
looking in frame.
is there a syntax to get around this. if it wernt a ggplot calculated
stat, you could do i in advance, but no so in this case.

thanks,
james

messages.author: 99a1cfc66539313c
messages.subject: Re: derived stats and variables not in frame
parts:
James

I have tried several things and couldn't solve this one either.

My proposed workaround is that you calculate the summary statistic
outside ggplot, and send the summarised data.frame to ggplot for
plotting only. As far as I know, stat_density() is based on the
loess() function.

Good luck.

Andrie

On Fri, Sep 24, 2010 at 6:02 AM, Ista Zahn <iz...@psych.rochester.edu> wrote:
This works:

library(ggplot2)
test.df <- data.frame(x=rnorm(10))
mult <- 2
ggplot(test.df, aes(x=x, y=(..density..)*get("mult",
envir=.GlobalEnv))) + geom_density()

-Ista

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: derived stats and variables not in frame
parts:
On Wed, Sep 22, 2010 at 9:34 PM, McCreight <mccr...@gmail.com> wrote:
> I appear to have troubles with the following conversion
>
> ggplot( frame, aes(x=x, y=(..density..)*2) )
>
> to
>
> mult=2
> ggplot( frame, aes(x=x, y=(..density..)*mult) )
>
> it complains that mult is not found. I assume that's because it's
> looking in frame.
> is there a syntax to get around this. if it wernt a ggplot calculated
> stat, you could do i in advance, but no so in this case.

Hmmm, this is a tricky issue because you want to evaluate mult in the
current environment, but ..density.. in the context of the transformed
data. One option would be to switch to aes_string: aes_string(x =
"x", y = paste("(..density..) * ", mult))

Hadley
